title: Enemy Spawn Weights
doc: Slice toggle. Off: Slices.VerdictForOverlay skips every file below before
it is opened, so none of its rows reach RulePlan. These files are loaded
by the row-edit engine, so they also have no effect while [Slices]
ModelRules is off (ModelRules.Init returns before Overlays.Load).
Files this toggle gates:
MonsterGroupMemberModel.spawn-corp-a.csv
MonsterGroupMemberModel.spawn-gang.csv
MonsterGroupMemberModel.spawn-syndicate.csv
MonsterGroupMemberModel.spawn-corp-c.csv
MonsterGroupMemberModel.spawn-fsc.csv
MonsterGroupMemberModel.spawn-bravestar.csv
MonsterGroupMemberModel.spawn-warnerbraun.csv
MonsterGroupMemberModel.spawn-ultratek.csv
MonsterGroupMemberModel.spawn-matsumoto.csv
MonsterGroupMemberModel.spawn-mckellen.csv
MonsterGroupMemberModel.spawn-jupiter.csv
MonsterGroupMemberModel.spawn-kemco.csv
WHAT IT IS FOR. One file per faction. A MonsterGroupMemberModel row ties
one enemy type to one spawn group and carries the weight that group rolls
it with, so editing a row's weight changes how often that enemy type is
rolled for a slot in that faction's opening roster at the power level the
row covers.
THE WEIGHTS ARE RELATIVE, NOT ABSOLUTE. A roll is made among the rows
eligible for the slot, so a weight only means anything next to the other
weights in the same faction. Doubling every weight in one file changes
nothing; doubling one of them changes that type's share.
THE BASELINE SCALE IS x100. The shipped numbers are written a hundred
times larger than the ratio they express, so a typical weight reads 200,
400 or 1000 rather than 2, 4 or 10. The headroom is deliberate: it is what
lets a weight be moved a little without rounding to nothing.
THERE IS NO FILE FOR A POOL NO GENERATED MISSION BUILDS. A faction whose
FactionModel.ProcGenSelect is 0 is never picked for a generated mission, and
a shared pool whose every user is such a faction is therefore never rolled.
The Corp shared pool (MonsterGroupId 500) is the one case: its only user is
Demo Corp. It carries no file, and the writer refuses rather than emitting
one for any pool that becomes unreachable in a later dump.
WHICH ROWS ARE IN A FILE. Each file carries its faction's weakest enemy
types, meaning the ones already eligible at power level 2 or below. The
stronger types the faction fields later are not in these files.
ONE ROW CARRIES ONE WEIGHT, so a weight that varies with power level is
written as several rows, each covering a single level. A row that covers
one power level is therefore the mechanism for making a weight
level-dependent, not a special case.
THE LOWEST-ENTERING TYPE TAPERS ONCE THE ROSTER IS FULL. Every pool
finishes unlocking types at some power level, and above that level no new
archetype enters and the band gates on a shipped row cannot be edited to
change that. So the type that enters lowest is thinned instead: its TOTAL
weight falls linearly from its x100 baseline at that last-unlock level to
1 at power level 20. Below the last-unlock level nothing changes, and
every other type keeps its x100 baseline and absorbs the share the lowest
type gives up.
AT POWER LEVEL 20 THE LOWEST TYPE HAS NO PER-LEVEL ROW. A per-level row
carries the total minus what that type's own shipped rows already
contribute, and at the end of the taper those are equal. A missing row at
the top of one ladder is the mechanism reaching its floor, not a gap.
Each file is a direct overlay: the part of the filename before the first
dot names the game table, and the "spawn-<faction>" part is the file's
tag. There is no expander: the first column is MonsterGroupMemberId, the
table's own id column, so overlay_kind_derived grades every one of these
files `direct` and the grid's first column grades `identity`.

This page sets how often each enemy type is rolled for a slot in that faction's opening roster, at each power level. There is one grid per faction.

The weights are relative, not absolute. A number only means something next to the other numbers in the same faction: doubling every weight in one grid changes nothing, and doubling one of them changes that type's share.
The baseline scale is x100, so a typical weight reads 200, 400 or 1000 rather than 2, 4 or 10. That headroom is on purpose - it is what lets you move a weight a little without it rounding to nothing.
Factions the game never picks for a generated mission have no grid here. There is one such case: the Corp shared pool, whose only user is Demo Corp.
Each grid names its faction's weakest enemy types. Weakest here means the ones already eligible at power level 2 or below.

One row carries one weight, so a weight that changes with power level is written as several rows, each covering a single level. A row that covers one power level is how a weight is made to vary with level.

The type that enters lowest - the baseline grunt - thins out over the late game. Once a faction has no more new enemy types to unlock, that grunt's weight falls in a straight line down to 1 at power level 20, and the other types take the share it gives up. Below that level the early-game mix is untouched.

fields.label: Enable Enemy Spawn Weights
fields.doc: On applies this slice's files; off skips them before they are opened. Default true. Twelve direct overlays onto MonsterGroupMemberModel, one per faction pool that a ProcGenSelect faction can field, each carrying that faction's weakest enemy types - the ones already eligible at power level 2 or below - and the weight each is rolled with at a given power level. The lowest-entering type in each faction tapers: its total weight falls linearly from its baseline at that faction's last-unlock power level to 1 at power level 20.
